content: If you are allergic to clindamycin, lincomycin, or any other substances, inform your doctor or pharmacist before using this medication. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as benzyl alcohol, which could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Clindamycin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Additionally, this medication can pass into breast milk, so consult your healthcare provider if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions can alter the way your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible drug interactions. Maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. While using this medication, your doctor may recommend laboratory or medical tests, such as kidney or liver function tests, to monitor your condition and ensure the medication is working safely. It is crucial to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, consult your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. For storage, refer to the product instructions or consult your pharmacist for specific details. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless explicitly instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in August 2024. It is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your health needs.
